---
title: "Lecture Notes for CMSC 424, Section 201, Spring 2026"
---

This contains a partial set of lecture notes, that were created automatically using the slides and audio transcripts, using AI tools (mostly Claude Code).

NOTE: I have not had a chance to carefully review the notes, which means there might errors or hallucinations. Also, the notes are not guaranteed to be complete and might be
missing things that were covered in class.

### Storage and Indexes

- [Computing and Storage Hardware](storage_1.qmd) — The storage hierarchy, access time orders of magnitude, CPUs and caches, hard disks, SSDs, and how hardware characteristics shape database system design.
- [File Organization](storage_2.qmd) — How tuples are laid out within blocks (fixed-length records, slotted pages, PAX) and across blocks (heap, sequential, hashing), plus column-oriented storage and columnar file formats like Parquet.
- [Indexes](storage_3.qmd) — B+-trees (structure, searching, insertion, deletion), log-structured merge trees, hash indexes, bitmap indexes, composite search keys, and R-trees.

### Query Processing and Optimization

- [Query Plans, Pipelining, and Cost](query_processing_1.qmd) — What a query plan is, logical vs physical operators, materialization vs pipelining, the iterator model (open/next/close), and how query cost is estimated.
- [Selection and Join Implementations](query_processing_2.qmd) — Sequential scan and index-based selection, nested loops join, index nested loops join, hash join, and hash-based outer joins (left, right, full).
- [Sort-Merge Join, Aggregation, and External Memory](query_processing_3.qmd) — Sort-merge join, group-by aggregation (hash-based and sort-based), duplicate elimination, set operations, and external memory algorithms (partitioned hash join and external sort-merge).
- [Introduction to Query Optimization](query_processing_4.qmd) — Why optimization matters, reading EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE output in PostgreSQL, secondary index thresholds, and how to use PostgreSQL hint parameters to force specific query plans.
- [Equivalence of Relational Expressions](query_processing_5.qmd) — Algebraic rewrite rules for selections, projections, and joins; selection pushdown (and when not to push); outer join restrictions; why full plan enumeration is infeasible.
- [Cost Estimation and Statistics](query_processing_6.qmd) — Selectivity estimation for equality and range predicates, most common values, histograms (equi-width and equi-depth), and what PostgreSQL stores in pg_stats.
- [Join Size Estimation and Optimization Algorithms](query_processing_7.qmd) — Join cardinality estimation (three cases), incorporating selections, heuristic optimization, and dynamic programming (Selinger algorithm).
- [Parallel and Distributed Architectures](query_processing_8.qmd) — Shared-memory, shared-disk, and shared-nothing architectures; speedup and scaleup; Amdahl's Law; hash and range partitioning; data replication; failure handling.
- [Parallel Execution of Relational Operators](query_processing_9.qmd) — Parallel sort (range-partition shuffle), parallel hash join, fragment-and-replicate join, and parallel aggregation (three scenarios based on group count and aggregate decomposability).

### Transactions

- [ACID Properties and Serializability](transactions_1.qmd) — What transactions are, ACID guarantees, schedules, serial vs serializable schedules, the precedence graph test for serializability.
- [Lock-Based Concurrency Control](transactions_2.qmd) — S/X locks, the lock manager, two-phase locking (2PL), strict 2PL, deadlock detection and prevention, multi-granularity locking with intention locks.
- [MVCC and Isolation Levels](transactions_3.qmd) — Timestamp-based ordering, optimistic concurrency control (OCC), snapshot isolation, write skew, and SQL isolation levels.
- [Recovery: Atomicity, Durability, and Logging](transactions_4_5.qmd) — Steal vs force policies, the memory/disk model, log-based recovery, write-ahead logging, UNDO with CLRs, REDO, the recovery algorithm, and checkpointing.
- [Distributed Transactions and Two-Phase Commit](transactions_6.qmd) — Distributed databases, data replication, quorum systems, failure modes in distributed settings, two-phase commit protocol, recovery scenarios, and connections to Paxos and blockchain consensus.
